result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (20 tests, 0 failures), and `bunx guren check` reports key parity for both locales.

I moved the sign-in and sign-up copy out of the page components into per-locale JSON catalogs and added Japanese. The English wording is now in `lang/en/auth.json` (verbatim from the old components, nested as `auth.login.*` / `auth.register.*`), with the matching Japanese in `lang/ja/auth.json` and the existing welcome message translated in `lang/ja/messages.json` (`:nameへようこそ！`, placeholder intact) — same files, same keys on both sides, which `bunx guren check` now verifies. `src/app.ts` declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'], fallback: 'en' }`, so the framework's built-in locale detection (`?locale=` → `locale` cookie → `Accept-Language`, restricted to the supported list) resolves `ja`/`ja-JP`/`ja-JP,ja;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.7` to Japanese and everything else — no header, `en`, `en-US,en;q=0.9,ja;q=0.5`, `fr-FR,fr;q=0.9` — to English. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` render every label, heading, button, and `<Head title>` through `useTranslation()` from `@guren/inertia-client`, and `LoginController.show` / `RegisterController.show` set their Inertia document title with `this.t('auth.<page>.title')` so the server-rendered `<title>` matches (`<title>ログイン</title>` with `<html lang="ja">` for a Japanese request, `Sign in` for English). Forms, validation, and redirects are untouched. New tests cover it: `tests/LoginController.test.ts` and `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` assert the resolved locale, the exact catalog shipped to the page, and the document title across all the header cases, using the small `tests/helpers/inertia.ts` payload reader; `tests/i18n.test.ts` guards catalog parity, placeholder survival, and that nothing is left untranslated. The convention is recorded in `docs/adr/0002-localize-auth-pages-with-per-locale-catalogs.md`.
